Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 94, verses 1–8:

This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–4} Allah, the Exalted, says, bestowing favour upon His Messenger: {Did We not expand for you your breast?}; that is, We widened it for the laws of the religion, the call to Allah, adorning oneself with noble character, turning towards the Hereafter, and facilitating good deeds. So it was not narrow or constricted, scarcely submitting to any good and scarcely finding any expansion. {And We removed from you your burden}; that is, your sin, {which had weighed down your back}; that is, made heavy, as Allah the Exalted said: {That Allah may forgive you your past and future sins} [48:2]. {And We raised high for you your mention}; that is, We elevated your standing and gave you a lofty, good renown that no one among creation has attained. Allah is not mentioned except that His Messenger – may Allah bless him and grant him peace – is mentioned along with Him, as in entering Islam, in the adhan (call to prayer), the iqamah (second call to prayer), the khutbahs (sermons), and other matters by which Allah elevated the mention of His Messenger Muhammad – may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He has in the hearts of his ummah (community) love, reverence and exaltation that no one else possesses after Allah, the Exalted. So may Allah reward him on behalf of his ummah with the best reward any prophet has been rewarded on behalf of his ummah.

{5–6} His saying: {So indeed, with hardship is ease. Indeed, with hardship is ease} [94:5–6] is a great glad tiding that whenever hardship and difficulty are found, ease accompanies it and goes along with it; even if hardship were to enter a lizard's burrow, ease would enter after it and bring it out, as Allah the Exalted said: {Allah will bring about after hardship ease} [65:7], and as the Prophet – may Allah bless him and grant him peace – said: "Indeed, relief comes with distress, and indeed, with hardship is ease."

The definiteness of "hardship" in the two verses indicates that it is one (the same hardship), while the indefiniteness of "ease" indicates its repetition; so one hardship will not overcome two eases.

Its definiteness with the article "al-" (alif and lam), which denotes totality and generality, indicates that every hardship, however severe its difficulty, has ease accompanying it at its end.

{7–8} Then Allah commanded His Messenger, primarily, and the believers, secondarily, to give thanks for Him and to fulfil the duty of His blessings, saying: {So when you have finished, then labour} [94:7]; that is, when you have freed yourself from your occupations and nothing remains in your heart that would hinder it, then strive in worship and supplication. {And to your Lord direct your longing} [94:8]: to Him alone; that is, with the utmost longing for the answering of your supplication and the acceptance of your prayers. Do not be among those who, when they are free, amuse themselves and turn away from their Lord and from His remembrance, and thus become among the losers.

It has been said that the meaning of this is: when you have finished the prayer and completed it, then labour in supplication, and to your Lord direct your longing in asking for your needs.

Whoever holds this view uses it as evidence for the legislated nature of supplication and remembrance (dhikr) following the obligatory prayers. And Allah knows best.

The end. And praise be to Allah.
